expectedRealization.rationale: The coordinated supply cut can lift crude realizations quickly, but integrated-company offsets and already-positive price breadth require company-level earnings confirmation before Primary.

acceptableExpressionSet.rationale: Sinopec has direct upstream oil exposure plus strong cash generation, but its refining/marketing businesses partially offset higher crude, so the new OPEC state is not a clean one-way earnings bridge.

changeHypothesis.summary: OPEC's first formal production cut since 2008 creates a genuinely new global supply state, but A-share integrated oil companies have offsetting upstream/refining economics and the frozen oil basket is already broadly positive.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: The cut is scheduled from Jan-2017 and can persist for months if compliance holds.
disconfirmingEvidence: Oil equities were already positive across both 20d and 60d windows.
Sinopec upstream remained loss-making while refining was highly profitable, creating offsetting sensitivity.
PetroChina still expected sharply lower 2016 profit.
COSL expected a large full-year loss and weak oil-service demand.

evidenceLedger.supportsClaim: A new coordinated global crude-supply cut was formally agreed.
Crude immediately repriced higher, showing rapid expectation absorption.
Sinopec has strong cash/overall earnings but sharply different upstream and refining economics.
Post-event valuation and oil-price EPS sensitivity were measurable before cutoff.
A direct upstream-heavy peer had a weak pre-event earnings baseline.
The broad oil basket was already favorable at cutoff.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: The frozen oil basket was about +4.30pp excess over 20d and +5.70pp over 60d with 100% positive breadth. A Dec-9 report placed Sinopec around 17x 2016E PE / 0.93x PB and already modeled a 2017 earnings recovery.
expectations.thesisExpectation: OPEC compliance raises crude enough to repair Sinopec upstream economics without erasing refining/marketing profitability.
expectations.measurableGap: The event is fresh and measurable, but the integrated offset plus broad price confirmation leaves only a Research-level residual gap.

expectationBurdenTest.valuationMethod: Contemporaneous PB/PE and explicit oil-price EPS sensitivity against frozen price absorption.
expectationBurdenTest.marketBaseline: A Dec-9 report already forecasts material 2017 EPS recovery under higher oil while the whole frozen oil basket is benchmark-positive.
expectationBurdenTest.thesisScenario: OPEC compliance sustains crude around/above the modeled baseline and upstream repair exceeds refining-spread compression.
expectationBurdenTest.breakevenCondition: Net integrated EPS must improve beyond the already-modeled recovery without requiring a further broad oil rerating.
expectationBurdenTest.ordinaryScenarioFailure: Compliance disappoints or refining-spread losses offset upstream gains.
expectationBurdenTest.catalystOrTimingBridge: OPEC implementation/compliance and Q4/Q1 segment earnings fall within the 60d base horizon.
